proof.text: Every finite-type $k$-scheme in the statement is Noetherian: a field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0,k$), and apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. A proper map is finite type by definition, and finite-type morphisms compose [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1). Compactification ambient schemes are consequently finite type over $k$, so the same Noetherian result applies to them. They are quasi-compact by the meaning of Noetherian and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) therefore makes all the tower arrows qcqs. In particular the proper factors meet the hypotheses of the named direct-image comparisons. Fix the notation $P_t^s=Rt_{s,*}$, $J_v^s=v_{s,!}$, and write $D^s_{t,u}:P_t^sP_u^s\to P_{tu}^s$ for the canonical compositor, the inverse of the comparison in [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition].

proof.text: The etale and pro-etale open extensions are exact, and $C_T=\nu_T^*$ is exact. Thus the sheaf isomorphism $e_v$ and its open-composition identities descend degreewise through localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The same applies to its open-unit normalization: it uses only exact open restrictions, open extensions and $C$. These equations therefore hold on $D^+$. In particular $e_{\mathrm{id}}=1$: its defining unit equation for the identity open says exactly this. On any fixed model $u=tv$, first apply $b_{t,J_v^eM}$, then $P_t^p(e_{v,M})$. These are isomorphisms and give exactly $c_u$ in the statement. Here $J_v^eM\in D^+$ and the comparison exhibits $F_u^pC M$ as the etale-origin object with witness $F_u^eM$.

Use [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] on the chosen compactifications of $f$ and $fh$. It supplies a compatible model
$$V\xrightarrow{i}\overline V\xrightarrow qW,\quad U\xrightarrow a\overline U\xrightarrow p\overline V,\quad H=\overline U\times_{\overline V}V,$$
with $b:H\hookrightarrow\overline U$, $r:H\to V$, $j:U\hookrightarrow H$, $bj=a$, $rj=h$, and Cartesian square $pb=ir$. The models for $h,f,fh$ are $(j,r),(i,q),(a,qp)$. Put $K=J_j^eL$. Write $\gamma^s:J_i^sP_r^s\to P_p^sJ_b^s$ for the proper/open map. On this tower [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] gives $\alpha^e=D^e E^e(P_q^e\gamma^e J_j^e)$ and specifies $\gamma^e$ as the adjoint of inverse open restriction. The new tower-normalization statement gives the same formula for the actual $\alpha^p$ with its open-adjoint $\gamma^p$, rather than taking that formula from a proof of another node. The ordinary general comparison covers both proper-factor cases; the narrower proper-composition lemma applies when the INNER factor $h$ is proper.

proof.text:
For $N\in D^+(H_e,\Lambda)$ set
$$S_N=J_i^p(b_{r,N})e_{i,P_r^eN},\qquad T_N=P_p^p(e_{b,N})b_{p,J_b^eN}.$$
Let $\lambda_N^s:i_s^*P_p^sJ_b^sN\to P_r^sN$ be open-restriction exchange followed by $P_r^s((\eta_b^s)^{-1})$. For $s=p$ its input is $C_HN$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] to $pb=ir$ at $J_b^eN$; its equation is precisely compatibility of the TWO exchange arrows with $a_i,a_b,b_p,b_r$. Postcompose with the inverse open-unit comparisons. Naturality of $b_r$ moves $(\eta_b^e)^{-1}$ through $b_r$, and the open-unit normalization for $e_b$ cancels $b_p^*e_b\,a_b\,C_H\eta_b^e=\eta_b^p$. Consequently
$$\lambda^p_{C_HN}\,i_p^*(T_N)\,a_{i,P_p^eJ_b^eN}=b_{r,N}\,C_V(\lambda^e_N).$$
All compositions are in $D^+(V_p,\Lambda)$; Step 2 supplies the derived open-unit equation. This is exchange compatibility on a proper, possibly nonfinite, Cartesian square.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, proper/open map, and 099R, comparison; explicit exchange/open-unit substitution

proof.text:
Take the two maps $\gamma^p_{C_HN}S_N$ and $T_NC_{\overline V}(\gamma^e_N)$ from $C_{\overline V}J_i^eP_r^eN$ to $P_p^pJ_b^pC_HN$. Precompose each with $e_{i,P_r^eN}^{-1}$ and transpose under $J_i^p\dashv i_p^*$. For the first, the transpose followed by $\lambda^p$ is $b_{r,N}$ by the defining transpose of $\gamma^p$. For the second, use the equation in Step 4 and the unit normalization for $e_i$; it becomes
$$b_{r,N}\,C_V(\lambda^e_N\,i_e^*(\gamma^e_N)\,\eta^e_{i,P_r^eN})=b_{r,N}.$$
The parenthesized map is the identity because the ordinary tower statement defines $\gamma^e$ as the adjunct of $(\lambda^e)^{-1}$. Since $\lambda^p$ is invertible and the adjunction is a bijection, the two maps agree:
$$\gamma^p_{C_HN}S_N=T_NC_{\overline V}(\gamma^e_N).$$
Thus this is an equality of the named mixed-site interchanges; separate naturality was not used in its place.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, adjoint normalization; explicit transpose computation

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal R=\alpha^p_{f,h,C_UL}F_f^p(c_{h,L})c_{f,F_h^eL}$. Expand the two $c$'s and the pro-etale tower formula at $K=J_j^eL$. In the following expression $D^pE^p$ denotes the final two compositors to $P_{qp}^pJ_a^p$, and juxtaposition is composition, read right to left. Naturality of $\gamma^p$ at the morphism $e_{j,L}:C_HK\to J_j^pC_UL$ (both objects of bounded-below etale origin), that is $\gamma^p_{J_j^pC_UL}\,J_i^pP_r^p(e_{j,L})=P_p^pJ_b^p(e_{j,L})\,\gamma^p_{C_HK}$, gives
$$\mathcal R=D^pE^p\,P_q^pP_p^pJ_b^p(e_{j,L})\,P_q^p(\gamma^p_{C_HK}J_i^p(b_{r,K})e_{i,P_r^eK})\,b_{q,J_i^eP_r^eK}.$$
Substitute Step 5, not an inferred interchange law. The parenthesized factor becomes $P_p^p(e_{b,K})b_{p,J_b^eK}C_{\overline V}(\gamma^e_K)$, so
$$\mathcal R=D^pE^p\,P_q^pP_p^p(J_b^p(e_j)e_{b,K})\,P_q^p(b_{p,J_b^eK})\,P_q^pC_{\overline V}(\gamma^e_K)\,b_{q,J_i^eP_r^eK}.$$
The first equality is naturality of the specified tower map; the second is the actual mixed square proved above.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, tower calculation; substitution of the named mixed-site interchange

proof.text:
Naturality of $b_q$ changes the last two factors of Step 6 to $b_{q,P_p^eJ_b^eK}\,C_W(P_q^e\gamma_K^e)$. The COMPOSITE law of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], with the counit-mate identification in [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange], is
$$D^p_{q,p}\,P_q^p(b_p)\,b_qP_p^e=b_{qp}\,C_W(D^e_{q,p}).$$
The open-composition law is
$$E^p_{b,j}\,(J_b^pe_j)\,(e_bJ_j^e)=e_a\,C_{\overline U}(E^e_{b,j}).$$
Use these two equations in the expanded expression, and naturality of the direct-image compositors to move the open factors through $D^p$. The result is
$$\mathcal R=P_{qp}^p(e_{a,L})\,b_{qp,J_a^eL}\,C_W(D^eE^e\,P_q^e\gamma^e_K)=c_{fh,L}C_W(\alpha^e_{f,h,L}).$$
This proves the equation on the compatible tower, with both compositors named. No compatibility of $b$ with composition is inferred from its naturality.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, four-line model calculation; 099R comparison composite law; 09AF open-comparison composite law

proof.text:
We next prove the required refinement square. For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, write $c_i=(j_i,t_i)$, so $t_1=t_2u$. Let $A_u^s:J_{j_2}^s\to P_u^sJ_{j_1}^s$ be the specified proper/open map, and put $T=P_u^p(e_{j_1})b_u$. [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization] states $A_u^pe_{j_2}=T C(A_u^e)$, hence
$$(A_u^p)^{-1}T=e_{j_2}C((A_u^e)^{-1}).$$
For the ordinary refinement statement, specialize its inner proper map to $\mathrm{id}$ and its outer map to the morphism being compactified; thus its refinement formula covers every morphism here. On bounded-below inputs the ordinary refinement comparisons of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] restrict, with the same normalization, to those of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], which are built from the map of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]; so the etale $A_u^e$ here is exactly the $\alpha^e_u$ of the site-normalization lemma, and $A_u^p$ is the pro-etale $\alpha_u$ used in [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism](a). The ACTUAL refinement maps, by [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism](b) on the pro-etale side and the normalized ordinary comparison statements on the etale side, are (up to taking inverses, which Step 9 allows)
$$\theta_u^s=P_{t_2}^s((A_u^s)^{-1})(D^s_{t_2,u})^{-1}.$$
We use these formulas, not just the separate cocycle laws on the two sites. The normalization lemma applies to this Noetherian proper/open square even when it is not Cartesian.

Apply the $b$ composite equation from Step 7 to $(t_2,u)$ and use naturality of $D$. With $b_{t_2}$ below evaluated at $P_u^eJ_{j_1}^eL$, expansion gives
$$\theta_u^pc^{c_1}=P_{t_2}^p((A_u^p)^{-1}T)\,b_{t_2}\,C((D^e_{t_2,u})^{-1}).$$
Substitute Step 8, then naturality of $b_{t_2}$ at $(A_u^e)^{-1}$:
$$\theta_u^pc^{c_1}=P_{t_2}^p(e_{j_2})\,b_{t_2,J_{j_2}^eL}\,C(P_{t_2}^e((A_u^e)^{-1})(D^e_{t_2,u})^{-1})=c^{c_2}C(\theta_u^e).$$
This proves the mixed refinement square. It also holds for inverse comparisons and finite composites, by multiplying the displayed equality by inverses and composing. Through a common refinement it therefore holds for every canonical comparison. Choose a common refining tower using the compatible-tower lemma. The separate compactification independence of the ordinary and pro-etale $\alpha$ maps now conjugates the equality of Step 7 to the originally chosen compactifications. This conjugation is legitimate because the mixed refinement square has just been proved.

proof.text: For a proper $u$ take $(\mathrm{id},u)$. Its two candidates are exactly $P_u^e$ and $P_u^p$ by the compact-support definitions. Step 2 gives $e_{\mathrm{id}}=1$, so the defining formula is $c_u=P_u^p(1)b_u=b_u$. If both factors are proper, choose all identity-open models: the tower square has identity horizontal arrows, its open-adjoint interchange is the identity, and the tower formula reduces to $D^s$; the required equation is exactly the $b$ composite equation of Step 7. For arbitrary compactifications use Step 9. The case with only $f$ proper is covered by the general ordinary tower formula, and that with $h$ proper agrees with the inner-proper normalization. We have used no assertion about composition maps from the proper base-change exchange corollary.

title: Site comparison preserves compact-support composition with a proper factor
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:U\to V$ and $f:V\to W$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and suppose at least one of $h,f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Choose compactifications of $h,f,fh$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $F_u^e=Ru^e_!$ for their small-etale compact-support functors [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $F_u^p=Ru^p_!$ for their small-pro-etale functors on bounded-below etale-origin objects [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Use their canonical compactification composition maps $\alpha^s_{f,h}:F_f^s F_h^s\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{fh}^s$ ($s=e,p$), obtained by proper/open interchange and ordinary direct-image composition [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition, lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition]. For proper factors their identification with ordinary direct image is the one from the identity-open compactification [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $u=tv$ with open $v$ and proper $t$, let
$$c_{u,M}=Rt_{p,*}(e_{v,M})\circ b_{t,v_{e,!}M}:C F_u^eM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_u^p C M,$$
where $b$ is the specified counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and $e$ is the canonical open-extension comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. For every $L\in D^+(U_e,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] the named maps satisfy
$$c_{fh,L}\circ C_W(\alpha^e_{f,h,L})=\alpha^p_{f,h,C_UL}\circ F_f^p(c_{h,L})\circ c_{f,F_h^eL}.$$
The same equality holds after any canonical refinement comparison; on a proper map $u$ its $c_u$ is $b_u$ under the identity-open identifications.

lean.note: All three clauses are named theorems: composition for arbitrary chosen compactifications with h proper OR f proper; the mixed square for the actual refinement map; and c=b under canonical identity-open proper identifications. Definitions assemble the specified canonical maps and bounded-below inclusion compatibilities. The added statement dependency is the already recorded refinement-comparison definition. No statement or split_report change.
